summary: This benchmark evaluates whether restoring the input signal of a grafted 7B coding module via an affine map transfers coding capabilities into a 14B host network. Through rigorous ablation controls across eight experimental arms and paired confidence intervals, the study documents a clean negative result where local signal recovery failed to yield donor-dependent full-network task completion.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including zero-output, affine approximation of native module, shuffled controls, and receiver ablation.
Precise architectural alignment and exact parameter verification (e.g., verifying the exact 275,268,608 parameter count of host block 28).
Thorough reporting of exact model revision commit hashes, hyperparameter settings, software environment versions, and hardware configuration.
Careful statistical analysis utilizing group-paired 95% confidence intervals and clearly articulated negative results.
weaknesses: Evaluated on only a single model architecture pair (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B into Qwen2.5-14B) and a single downstream syntax-completion task panel.
Calibration was fitted exclusively at a single prediction position token before being applied uniformly across all sequence positions.
No standalone repository was attached directly as supporting code for the benchmark review, relying on embedded external commit links.
suggestions: Expand evaluation beyond bracket matching to more diverse code repair and generation benchmarks (e.g., HumanEval or MultiPL-E).
Test multi-position sequence calibration rather than single-token prediction position fitting to isolate downstream context mismatch.
Explore multi-layer adaptation budgets rather than restricting gradient updates strictly to receiver block 28.

claims.text: The donor is Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base at revision 0396a76181e127dfc13e5c5ec48a8cee09938b02.
The host is Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B base at revision 97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9.
An affine transform maps host pre-module activations from 5,120 to 3,584 coordinates.
The 275,268,608 parameters of block 28 alone receive gradients.
